claims.claim: Clement of Alexandria (c. 147 – c. 215 AD) was a Christian theologian and head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria.
He was born in Alexandria or Athens and died in Jerusalem, serving as a leading teacher of the early Church.
The work titled “To the Newly Baptized” (also called “Exhortation to Endurance”) is a short address attributed to Clement and was composed around AD 200.
It was written as a catechetical exhortation giving moral instructions to recent converts, urging quietness, self‑control, prayer, and proper conduct.
The address is directed specifically to newly baptized Christians.
The fragment was once thought lost but has been recovered and is now available in digital editions.
